facts.assertion: Enfield's new Local Plan covers the period 2019 to 2039.
Enfield states it is working on the new Local Plan to shape future development in the borough.
Enfield's most recent call for sites ran in June/July 2022 and closed on 15 July 2022.
Enfield says land availability will continue to be kept under annual review until the plan is adopted.
Enfield describes call for sites as an early opportunity to suggest land available for development.
Enfield says call-for-sites submissions inform preparation of the new Local Plan.
Enfield explicitly says the call for sites does not determine whether a site should be allocated.
Enfield says call-for-sites submissions form a potential pool for further technical assessment.
Enfield says publication of a submitted site does not indicate that it will be allocated.
Enfield says publication of a submitted site does not indicate it will successfully obtain planning permission.
Enfield says sites are tested for suitability, availability and achievability.
Enfield says housing and employment sites are considered through the HELAA.
Enfield states the plan and associated sites go through independent examination before adoption.
The emerging Enfield Local Plan was approved for Regulation 19 publication by Full Council on 19 March 2024.
The Regulation 19 consultation ran from 28 March to 20 May 2024.
Enfield submitted the Local Plan to the Secretary of State for examination on 6 August 2024.
Enfield's current Local Plan page labels the process Regulation 24 2024 – Examination in Public.
Enfield's Regulation 19 document list includes Appendix C Site Allocations.
Enfield's Regulation 19 document list includes a policies map and plan chapters.
Enfield's examination library includes proposed modifications and updated housing trajectory evidence.
On 15 June 2026 the Planning Inspector issued a post-hearing letter to Enfield Council.
Enfield says the Inspector's 15 June 2026 letter sets out further Main Modifications or steps required for soundness and legal compliance.
Enfield reports that the Inspector recommended removal of certain development sites from the Green Belt.
Enfield states the Council would review the Inspector's findings before determining next steps.
Enfield's Local Plan page lists a council response to the Inspector's post-hearing letter dated 29 June 2026.
Enfield's Local Plan page still presents the plan as Examination in Public after the June 2026 post-hearing correspondence.
The examination stage is not the same as adoption of the new Enfield Local Plan.
A Regulation 19 site-allocation appendix is plan-stage evidence, not exact parcel membership for candidate 30762.
A call-for-sites submission is not an allocation according to Enfield's own guidance.
HELAA consideration is not equivalent to an adopted allocation according to Enfield's plan-making sequence.
The Inspector's recommendation about some Green Belt sites does not identify candidate row 30762 without geometry or site-reference binding.
The current Enfield plan stage requires temporal guarding before any future-growth score promotion.
Candidate row 30762 remains unbound to a borough-confirmed positive allocation polygon.
The new GLA layer-102 envelope exclusion for row 30762 does not replace borough-specific Enfield geometry verification.
Enfield's plan-stage documents can be used to classify source currentness but not to infer point-in-polygon membership.
An adopted allocation would still require planning permission for a development proposal; allocation and planning permission are distinct concepts in Enfield's published guidance.
Enfield's call-for-sites material explicitly distinguishes potential development land from sites ultimately selected for allocation.
No positive candidate binding is inferred from the 2026 post-hearing letter because it is not a parcel-level spatial query result.
No negative borough binding is inferred from the GLA indicative layer exclusion because GLA directs users to boroughs for boundary accuracy.
Business score for candidate 30762 remains unchanged pending authoritative borough geometry execution.
